newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains excessive in some Brazil soybean areas - coops.
newsitem.headline: Rains excessive in some Brazil soybean areas - coops.

text.p: Scattered rains continued to fall in Brazil's key soybean growing regions, but growers in Parana said their crops might suffer if the heavy rainfall there continued for much longer.

While farmers in Rio Grande do Sul rejoiced over rains that are restoring soil moisture to normal levels, those in neighbouring Parana were looking at cloudy skies and praying for a few days of sunshine.
"It's rained too much," said Edson Luiz de Soza, agronomist at the Copagril cooperative in Marechal Candido Rondon. "We can't talk about any crop loss yet because it's only affecting isolated spots."
Patches of the crop were suffering from fungi and more rain was on the cards later today and at the end of the week. "If it continues for a few more days then we will have a problem," said de Soza.
"Soil moisture is excessive," agreed Luiz Antonio Bittencourt, agronomist at the Bom Jesus cooperative in Lapa. "We've had a small crop loss of around five percent."
Temperatures were moderate at 25 to 28 degrees Celsius but less rain was needed, he said.
In Rio Grande do Sul, conditions were near-ideal and independent meteorologist Somar predicted another cold front would reach the region on February 5.
"Soil moisture is normal," said Sergio Gregory at the Santa Barbara cooperative.
Between 80 and 85 percent of the crop was in the flowering phase and temperatures were around 30 degrees C, he said.
